elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted § 2(e): "Client owns all deliverables and work product created for Client under this Agreement, including all results of the Support Services" — direct customer-side ownership statement, in Client's favour.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: "...and TrueLink hereby assigns all right, title and interest therein to Client" — present-tense assignment of the deliverables/work product just defined.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained § 2(d): "TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface," and the new licence-back sentence ("any TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in such deliverables") presupposes continued TrueLink ownership of that pre-existing IP rather than assigning it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any TrueLink Intellectual Property embedded in such deliverables and work product." The licence is expressly perpetual and, being a standalone grant in § 2(e), is not subject to the § 2(c) term limitation that applies to "[t]he license" granted under § 2(a).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content, Client Intellectual Property and all borrower and loan data." This tracks the data descriptors already used in the document ("Client Content" in § 13; "borrower and loan data" in the confidentiality list) and is not displaced by the § 8(d) archived Credit Data grant, which is a licence only.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "No intellectual property will be jointly owned by the parties." No joint-ownership language exists elsewhere to contradict it.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Retained § 2(d) leaves TrueLink's ownership of the Interface (its platform/tooling) intact, and the redline does not disturb it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Subsumed and exceeded: § 2(e) vests outright ownership of the deliverables in Client, so no time-limited licence applies; the embedded-vendor-IP grant is separately stated as perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Ownership of "all right, title and interest" in the deliverables cannot be revoked; the embedded-IP grant is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Client's ownership of the deliverables carries no territorial limit, but the embedded TrueLink IP grant is "perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free" with no "worldwide" qualifier; on a literal reading the fallback territorial term is absent from operative language.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Ownership requires no royalty, and the embedded-IP grant is expressly royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership of all right, title and interest in the deliverables includes use and modification; no retained sentence restricts modification of work product.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Client's ownership of the deliverables permits onward licensing, but no sublicence right is stated for embedded TrueLink Intellectual Property, so a deliverable containing embedded vendor IP could not literally be sublicensed under the § 2(e) grant.

elements.element: Cross-check: no assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor survives (walk-away).
elements.evidence: Deterministic check confirms no remaining Client-to-TrueLink assignment; § 8(d) is a licence over narrowly defined archived Credit Data and § 2(e) preserves Client's retained title.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the inserted § 2(e) supplies Client ownership plus express TrueLink assignment of deliverables/work product (including Support Services results), a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP, retention of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property and borrower and loan data, and an express no-joint-ownership sentence; vendor pre-existing IP retention is already met by the untouched § 2(d).

Fallback level is not independently complete (missing "worldwide" and any sublicence right for embedded TrueLink IP), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is satisfied and ownership is the stronger outcome.

Minimal: a single concise insertion, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, no added damages or indemnity mechanics, and the favourable retained § 2(d) vendor-ownership sentence and § 13 domain/Client Content ownership language are left in place. No operative term is duplicated.

Preserves intent: the § 2(a) Interface licence, § 2(c) term, § 8(d) archived Credit Data licence and § 13 term/discontinuation mechanics all survive without contradiction, since the new clause addresses only work product created for Client and expressly presupposes TrueLink's ownership of embedded IP.

Drafting nit (not a defect requiring repair): "TrueLink Intellectual Property" and "Client Intellectual Property" are capitalised but only quasi-defined in the confidentiality list; consider lower-casing or cross-referencing so no reader treats them as undefined defined terms.
Optional hardening if the counterparty resists ownership: add "worldwide" and "sublicensable" to the embedded-IP licence so the fallback position is also independently satisfied.
